_hinweis: Content for /syllabus (src/pages/kursinhalte.astro, src/pages/kursinhalte/[level].astro, src/components/KursProgression.astro) and the lesson-plan generator (src/lib/stundenplan.js, which links each grammar line to a topic page by the patterns in GRAMMAR_RULES, so keep the wording of a grammar line close to the topic's name). Everything here is our own, written from the CEFR can-do descriptors. Never copy from coursebooks or from the Plan Curricular: no unit titles, no tables of contents, no texts. `lehrwerke` would name coursebook series only ("goes with"), without a level after the name; the lists are empty until Edgar decides whether to name any (scripts/check-lehrwerk-leak.mjs fails the build on series + level). To add a level: insert an object in `niveaus` (order = order on the page and in the timeline); the id becomes the URL (/syllabus/<id>). `pruefung` from A2.2 (DELE, SIELE; see docs/content-plan.md §2): name the exam and the skill, never a task number, a timing or a word count, because those facts are unverified until the exam items check them. `selbstcheck`: exactly 5 sentences describing what a learner can do BEFORE this level.

probestunde._hinweis: Empty = an email to the contact address in src/lib/legal.js (there is no booking page yet). Once there is one, put its path here, e.g. "/probestunde". {niveau} is replaced by the level.

niveaus.label: A1.1
niveaus.ziel: You talk about yourself, your family and your day, in simple sentences.

kannZiele: You can introduce yourself: name, country, languages.
You can ask other people their name and where they are from.
You can spell your name.
grammatik: Subject pronouns: yo, tú, usted, vosotros
ser and estar: soy, eres, es; estoy, estás, está
Question words: qué, quién, dónde, de dónde

kannZiele: You can say your phone number, address and age.
You can fill in a simple form.
grammatik: Numbers up to 1,000
Yes/no questions: ¿Eres…? ¿Tienes…?
Key irregular verbs: tener (tengo 30 años)

kannZiele: You can introduce your family.
You can say who belongs to you and how old they are.
grammatik: Possessives: mi, tu, su
Nouns and gender: el hermano, la hermana
Plurals: hijos, padres, jóvenes

kannZiele: You can describe your flat and your furniture.
You can say what is in your home and where it is.
grammatik: Articles: el, la, un, una
hay or está: Hay un sofá. El sofá está aquí.
Adjectives: agreement (la cocina pequeña)

kannZiele: You can ask for products and prices in a shop.
You can order in a bar.
You can write a shopping list.
grammatik: Articles: unos, unas (unos tomates)
Polite requests: quería…, ¿me pone…?
Demonstratives: este, ese, aquel
Question words: ¿cuánto cuesta?
wortschatz: Containers (una botella de, un paquete de)

kannZiele: You can describe your daily routine with times.
You can say how often you do something.
grammatik: Present tense: regular -ar, -er, -ir verbs
Telling the time: a las ocho, por la mañana
Reflexive verbs: me levanto, me ducho (first look)
Frequency: siempre, a veces, nunca (first look)

kannZiele: You can talk about your hobbies.
You can say what you like and what you don't like.
You can ask others what they do in their free time.
grammatik: gustar: me gusta, me gustan
Stem-changing verbs: quiero, puedo, juego
Yes/no questions and negation with no: No trabajo hoy.
Linking words: y, o, pero, porque

selbstcheck: I can read and write the letters of the Latin alphabet.
I know a few words in Spanish (hola, gracias, sí, no).
I can say my name in Spanish.
I know the numbers from 1 to 10 in Spanish.
I have some time each week to practise at home.
niveaus.selbstcheckNiedrig: No problem: A1.1 is the beginning, you don't need to know anything yet. In the trial lesson we look together at the best way for you to start.

niveaus.label: A1.2
niveaus.ziel: You get by in everyday life: in town, at the health centre, in shops and at the town hall.

kannZiele: You can ask the way and understand simple directions.
You can buy a ticket for the bus, the metro or the train.
grammatik: Key irregular verbs: ir, venir, salir
a or en: voy a Madrid, estoy en Madrid
Saying where: al lado de, enfrente de, entre
Question words: ¿Cómo voy a…? ¿Dónde está…?

kannZiele: You can say what hurts at the health centre.
You can understand simple advice and instructions.
grammatik: gustar and doler: me duele la cabeza
tener que, hay que, poder
Possessives or article: me duele la pierna

bloecke.thema: What are you doing? What will you do?
kannZiele: You can say what you are doing right now.
You can talk about your plans.
You can say what you have done today.
grammatik: estar + gerund: estoy trabajando
ir a + infinitive: voy a llamar
Pretérito perfecto: first steps (hoy he comido)

kannZiele: You can say what you do and where you work.
You can describe your working day.
grammatik: ser and estar: soy enfermera, estoy en paro
Article or no article: Soy enfermera.
Key irregular verbs: hacer, saber, conocer

kannZiele: You can ask for clothes in a shop and try them on.
You can compare two things.
grammatik: Comparatives: más… que, menos… que
Direct object pronouns: lo, la (¿Lo tiene en azul?)
Demonstratives: este, esa, aquellos
Adjectives: colours and agreement

kannZiele: You can say the date and when something happens.
You can invite someone and accept or say no.
grammatik: Ordinal numbers and dates: el 3 de mayo
Telling the time and days: el lunes, los lunes
ir a + infinitive for plans

kannZiele: You can make an appointment and ask for a form.
You can give your details at a counter (town hall, bank, health centre).
grammatik: Polite requests: ¿Puede…? Quería…
Yes/no questions and short answers: Sí, claro. No, todavía no.
Numbers: letters and numbers of an NIE, phone numbers

selbstcheck: I can introduce myself and ask others their name and where they are from.
I can understand numbers, prices and the time.
I can talk about my family.
I can ask for things in a shop.
I can describe my day with times.

niveaus.label: A2.1
niveaus.ziel: You talk about the past, give reasons for your opinion and get by well when you travel.

kannZiele: You can say what your life was like before.
You can talk about what you used to do.
grammatik: Pretérito imperfecto: antes vivía, era, iba
Frequency: soler + infinitive
Comparatives: más que antes

kannZiele: You can say what you did yesterday or last year.
You can tell a short story from your life.
grammatik: Pretérito indefinido: hablé, comí, fui
Pretérito perfecto: ya, todavía no, esta semana
Pretérito indefinido: ayer, el año pasado, hace dos años

kannZiele: You can describe a flat and say where things are.
You can talk to a neighbour or a landlord about a small problem.
grammatik: Saying where: encima de, debajo de, detrás de
a or en: going and being
Indefinites: algo, nada, alguien, nadie

kannZiele: You can explain why you do something.
You can say what you have to do at work.
grammatik: porque, como, así que, por eso; creo que
tener que, hay que, deber
Indirect object pronouns: le doy, me pagan

kannZiele: You can say how much you like something.
You can describe how you do things.
grammatik: muy, mucho, poco, bastante, demasiado
Adverbs: -mente; bien or bueno
gustar: a mí también, a mí tampoco

kannZiele: You can compare habits and say what is better.
You can talk about your routine and your health.
grammatik: Comparatives and superlatives: tan… como, el mejor
Reflexive verbs: me cuido, me acuesto tarde
Negation: no, nunca, tampoco, nada

kannZiele: You can plan a trip and book a room.
You can pass things on and say who gets what.
grammatik: ir a + infinitive for trips
Indirect object pronouns: se lo doy
Direct object pronouns: lo, la, los, las; personal a

selbstcheck: I can say what I did at the weekend.
I can ask the way and understand the answer.
I can tell a doctor what hurts.
I can make or cancel an appointment.
I can say in a shop what I like and what fits me.

niveaus.label: A2.2
niveaus.ziel: You describe people and things in more detail, give advice and deal with offices and work. This is the level of the DELE A2, the language certificate usually asked for on the path to Spanish nationality.

kannZiele: You can tell someone about a festival or a party.
You can say when things happened.
grammatik: Pretérito indefinido: fui, tuve, hice, dije
Ordinal numbers and dates
Key irregular verbs: review

kannZiele: You can describe what someone is like.
You can say what you have in common.
grammatik: Article or no article: Me gusta el café. Tengo coche.
Adjectives: agreement and position
Comparatives: tan… como, tanto como

kannZiele: You can ask for help and offer it.
You can give simple advice.
grammatik: deber and tener que for advice
Polite requests: me gustaría, ¿te importa…?
Reflexive verbs: review

kannZiele: You can pay, return a product and complain politely.
You can read a bill and understand the main charges.
grammatik: Direct object pronouns: lo devuelvo, la pago; personal a
Indefinites: algún, ningún, otro
Indirect object pronouns: se lo mando

kannZiele: You can talk about the weather and the seasons in Spain.
You can say what you do for the environment.
grammatik: muy, mucho, demasiado: review
Pretérito imperfecto: describing the weather and the place
Negation: nadie, ninguno, double negation

kannZiele: You can talk about your work experience.
You can answer simple questions in an interview.
grammatik: Pretérito perfecto and pretérito indefinido in your CV
porque, como, por eso
Saying how often: siempre, a menudo, soler

kannZiele: You can explain what you need at an office (padrón, NIE, health card) and understand what to bring.
You can ask someone to repeat or to write something down.
grammatik: Polite requests: ¿Podría…? Quería…
Direct object pronouns: ¿Lo traigo? ¿La firmo?
Ordinal numbers: la primera planta, el segundo piso

selbstcheck: I can talk about my childhood.
I can give reasons with porque and como.
I can ask politely: ¿Puede…? Quería…
I can compare things: más grande que, el mejor.
I can talk about my hobbies (me interesa, me gusta).

niveaus.label: B1.1
niveaus.ziel: You talk about experiences, plans and opinions, also on topics that are less familiar.

kannZiele: You can tell the story of your life or of a journey in the right order.
You can describe the background of an event.
grammatik: Indefinido or imperfecto: telling a story
Pluscuamperfecto: había comido
Time: desde, desde hace, hace… que, hasta, durante

kannZiele: You can talk about your experience and your plans at work.
You can write a short email to a company.
grammatik: Perfecto or indefinido: hoy he ido, ayer fui
Verbal periphrases: acabar de, volver a, dejar de, llevar
Relative clauses: que, donde, lo que

kannZiele: You can say what you think about the news and social media.
You can give arguments for and against.
grammatik: Linkers: aunque, sin embargo, además
Verbs + prepositions: pensar en, depender de

kannZiele: You can follow a doctor's instructions and ask for details.
You can tell someone what to do and what not to do.
grammatik: Imperative: toma, no tomes, tómalo
Verbs like gustar: doler, molestar, parecer

kannZiele: You can sort out a problem with a landlord or flatmates.
You can say what would be better.
grammatik: Real conditions: si + present
Condicional simple: me gustaría, yo que tú
Pronouns after prepositions: para mí, conmigo

kannZiele: You can talk about plans and predictions.
You can solve a problem while travelling.
grammatik: Futuro simple: hablaré, tendré
por or para: salgo para Sevilla, paso por Toledo

kannZiele: You can talk about relationships and what people are like.
You can say whose something is.
grammatik: ser and estar: when the meaning changes
Possessive pronouns: el mío, la tuya

selbstcheck: I can talk about past events with the indefinido and the perfecto.
I can give advice: Tienes que… Deberías…
I can describe people and things in simple sentences with que.
I can write a simple email to a company.
I can say when something happened with cuando and después de.

niveaus.label: B1.2
niveaus.ziel: You discuss, describe processes and write clear texts, and you are ready for a B1 exam.

kannZiele: You can say what you hope and what you want others to do.
You can discuss what should change.
grammatik: Present subjunctive: the forms (hable, coma, tenga, vaya)
Subjunctive after wishes and feelings: espero que, ojalá

kannZiele: You can talk about courses and qualifications.
You can say what something is for.
grammatik: Infinitive or subjunctive: quiero ir, quiero que vayas
Purpose: para + infinitive, para que + subjunctive

kannZiele: You can report what other people say.
You can ask for information politely.
grammatik: Indirect questions and reporting: dice que, me pregunta si, no sé dónde
Relative clauses: lo que, donde

kannZiele: You can compare offers and make a complaint.
You can talk about what is on sale and what is closed.
grammatik: estar + participle: la tienda está cerrada
Adjective position and short forms: buen, gran
Word formation: -ción, -dad, -ero, -ería

kannZiele: You can talk about what will happen when things change.
You can write a formal email or a complaint.
grammatik: Time clauses: cuando llegue, en cuanto, hasta que
lo + adjective: lo importante es, lo que

kannZiele: You can talk about films, books and events.
You can recommend something and say why.
grammatik: Verbs + prepositions: soñar con, acordarse de, tardar en
Verbs like gustar: encantar, interesar, quedar

kannZiele: You know the format of the exam you want to take and can manage your time.
You can do a full practice test.
grammatik: Review: past tenses and time clauses
Review: subjunctive and conditions
wortschatz: Useful phrases for writing and speaking

selbstcheck: I can tell a story in the right order (primero, después, mientras).
I can give my opinion and support it with aunque and sin embargo.
I can use the present subjunctive after quiero que and espero que.
I can write a complaint or a formal email.
I can plan a meeting or a trip with other people.

niveaus.label: B2.1
niveaus.ziel: You understand longer texts, argue convincingly and write in a formal style, at work and in study.

kannZiele: You can discuss working conditions and give reasons for your view.
You can write a formal letter of application.
grammatik: Subjunctive in opinion and doubt: no creo que, es posible que
Collocations: tomar una decisión, dar un paseo

kannZiele: You can follow a news report and say what it means.
You can report what was said.
grammatik: Passive and se: se dice, se alquila, fue aprobado
Reported speech with tense shifts: dijo que vendría

kannZiele: You can describe the housing market where you live.
You can say exactly what you are looking for.
grammatik: Relative clauses with subjunctive: busco un piso que tenga…
Concession and consequence: aunque + subjunctive

kannZiele: You can talk about stress, moods and how people change.
You can tell someone about a small accident or a mistake.
grammatik: Verbs of change: ponerse, volverse, quedarse
Accidental se: se me olvidó, se me ha roto

kannZiele: You can talk about what would be different under other conditions.
You can say what you wanted other people to do.
grammatik: Imperfect subjunctive: quería que vinieras
Unreal conditions: si tuviera, compraría

kannZiele: You can read a contract or terms and ask about the details.
You can explain results and effects.
grammatik: Adjectives + prepositions: harto de, capaz de, interesado en
Concession and consequence: tan… que, de modo que

kannZiele: You can keep a conversation going and interrupt politely.
You can guess what has happened and say how sure you are.
grammatik: Discourse markers in speech: pues, bueno, o sea, es que
Probability: serán las tres, habrá salido

selbstcheck: I have finished B1 or feel confident at B1.
I can use the present subjunctive for wishes and feelings.
I can link ideas with aunque, sin embargo and por lo tanto.
I can give a talk on a topic for 3–4 minutes.
I understand the main points of the news on the radio.

niveaus.label: B2.2
niveaus.ziel: You write and speak precisely, also about abstract topics, and you are ready for a B2 exam.

kannZiele: You can discuss scenarios and what could happen.
You can weigh up possible solutions.
grammatik: Probability: future and conditional of conjecture
Unreal conditions: si hubiera…, habría… (introduction)

kannZiele: You can summarise a report in your own words.
You can describe processes in a formal style.
grammatik: Passive and se: se ha demostrado, fue descubierto
Nominalisation in formal writing (introduction)

kannZiele: You can explain how decisions are made in Spain.
You can report requests and demands.
grammatik: Reported speech with tense shifts: me pidió que fuera
Subjunctive in opinion and doubt: dudo que, no es verdad que

kannZiele: You can talk about belonging, languages and customs.
You can describe how a person or a place has changed.
grammatik: Relative clauses with prepositions: el piso en el que vivo, quien
Verbs of change: hacerse, convertirse en

kannZiele: You can write a report or a review.
You can say what you would have liked to happen.
grammatik: Imperfect subjunctive: me gustaría que, ojalá pudiera
Collocations: hacer caso, poner una queja, echar de menos

kannZiele: You can discuss a rule or a law and say what you think of it.
You can make a formal complaint.
grammatik: Concession and consequence: por mucho que, aunque
Adjectives + prepositions: contento con, responsable de

kannZiele: You know the format of the exam you want to take and can manage your time.
You can do a full practice test.
grammatik: Review: subjunctive and conditions
Review: reported speech and linkers
wortschatz: Useful phrases for writing and speaking

selbstcheck: I can write formal emails without help.
I understand the imperfect subjunctive when I read it.
I can report what someone said (dijo que…).
I can disagree in a discussion and suggest a compromise.
I understand newspaper articles on familiar topics.

niveaus.label: C1
niveaus.ziel: You understand demanding texts, speak spontaneously and fluently, and write well-structured texts.

kannZiele: You can understand long factual texts and summarise them.
You can present results in a formal style.
grammatik: Nominalisation in formal writing
Sequence of tenses with the subjunctive; hubiera hecho

kannZiele: You can write a report or a proposal.
You can lead a meeting and sum up.
grammatik: Non-finite clauses: al llegar, viendo que…, terminada la reunión
Formal connectors: debido a, a raíz de

kannZiele: You can argue about abstract topics and answer counter-arguments.
You can set conditions and limits precisely.
grammatik: Conditions without si: de + infinitive, a no ser que, siempre que
Formal relatives: el cual, lo cual, cuyo

kannZiele: You can tell fact from opinion in a long article or a programme.
You can put the focus exactly where you want it.
grammatik: Emphasis and cleft sentences: Fue Ana quien…, Lo que necesito es…
Modal periphrases: deber de, venir a, llegar a

kannZiele: You can talk about how language varies in Spain and the Spanish-speaking world.
You can switch between formal and informal style.
grammatik: Prefixes and derivation: des-, re-, pre-, in-, sobre-
Discourse markers and register

kannZiele: You can explain complex causes and effects.
You can turn a spoken explanation into formal writing.
grammatik: Nominalisation and verbal style: decidir, la decisión
Formal connectors: no obstante, por consiguiente, en virtud de

kannZiele: You can write a review and give a nuanced opinion.
You can follow a discussion about a film or a book.
grammatik: como si + subjunctive; ni que
Cohesion: reference, ellipsis, lo and ello

kannZiele: You know the format of the exam you want to take and can manage your time.
You can do a full practice test.
grammatik: Review: formal style and sentence structure
Review: subjunctive and sequence of tenses
wortschatz: Useful phrases for writing and speaking

selbstcheck: I have finished B2 or feel confident at B2.
I can report what other people said, with the right tenses.
I can argue about abstract topics and give counter-arguments.
I understand factual texts and talks on most topics.
I can switch between a formal and an informal style.
